reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency arbitrage opportunity by claiming that viewers can earn $250 in a few minutes through a 12% to 15% spread. It gives a concrete participation flow involving deposits, transfers between Binance and Trade-CRYPTO, selling ADA, withdrawing USDT, and paying a $1 fee. It also urges viewers to act before the method stops working, although the material does not establish that any transfer completed or profit was realized.

citations.quote: The result of this video is that it clearly showed you how I earned 250$ in a few minutes with one trade.
Buy on Binance - https://binance.com/ Sell on Trade-CRYPTO - https://zelaxce.com
15% PROFIT FROM ONE CIRCLE
Let's Start with a small amount to get the jest of it
We bought it with 1 euro

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful qualification rather than a blanket promise. It expressly says the opportunity "will not work forever," which communicates that the conditions are temporary and uncertain, even while recommending timely use. It also frames the material as a personal tutorial and says to begin with a small amount. That combination is more consistent with a risk-qualified demonstration of a trading opportunity than with a guaranteed-return solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes the claimed percentages and urgency, but those points do not erase the explicit qualification that the method is temporary. The supplied screen also shows a withdrawal still marked pending, so the material does not establish a completed, guaranteed outcome. At most, it presents a conditional opportunity with a stated limitation.

citations.quote: know that it will not work forever, so I recommend using it as soon as possible.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning that the method may stop working does not make the promotion non-deceptive when the same description claims personal earnings and advertises a 15% return. Saying to start small limits initial exposure but still directs viewers toward a money-transfer workflow. The qualification is therefore compatible with a risky scam promotion, not a reliable safeguard.

opening.argument: The central format is an operational tutorial and personal demonstration. The description calls it a tutorial, while the narration walks through buying, selling, and withdrawing in sequence. The sampled frames likewise show exchange interfaces and captions directing the next step. That evidence supports treating the video as instruction about how an arbitrage process is performed, rather than as proof that viewers are being promised a particular financial result.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling something a tutorial does not answer what the tutorial promotes. This one names the platforms, describes a spread, and instructs viewers to move funds and sell coins. The instructional format makes the participation path clearer; it does not by itself convert the advertised earnings claim into neutral commentary.

citations.quote: Buy on Binance - https://binance.com/ Sell on Trade-CRYPTO - https://zelaxce.com
Our Spread is 12%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstrated workflow is not merely abstract education: it is paired with a claim that the creator earned $250 in minutes and with a stated profit percentage. Showing operational steps can be the mechanism by which viewers are induced to participate. The tutorial label does not establish that the named destination or the displayed outcome is genuine or reproducible.

opening.argument: The material describes ordinary exchange activity: buying on Binance and selling on another named trading service. The visible evidence is a trading screen, an address field, and a withdrawal interface marked as processing. It does not show a downline, recruitment scheme, credential request, or guaranteed-return contract. A stated spread or profit figure may be an optimistic performance claim, but the supplied evidence does not establish the characteristic mechanism of a guaranteed or recruitment-based scam.

citations.quote: Buy on Binance - https://binance.com/ Sell on Trade-CRYPTO - https://zelaxce.com

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account identifies a transfer workflow, but transferring assets between trading venues is also consistent with ordinary arbitrage. Its own description says the material does not establish that a transfer completed or profit was realized. The visible withdrawal status is pending, which weakens rather than proves the claim that a fraudulent return mechanism operated.

citations.quote: Funds came back with a $1 fee!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Ordinary-looking interfaces do not make the advertised service ordinary or safe. The video directs viewers to buy on one platform, sell on another, transfer assets, and pursue a claimed 12% to 15% return. The pending withdrawal and blurred destination do not verify completion; they instead leave the central earnings claim unsupported while still presenting a concrete participation route.
